question: In which athletics event did Eldhose Paul win a gold medal at the Commonwealth Games 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Triple Jump.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Eldhose Paul won a gold medal in the men's Triple Jump at the Commonwealth Games 2022 (Birmingham), becoming the first Indian to win a CWG gold in the triple jump. (एल्डहॉस पॉल — ट्रिपल जंप)

• Fellow Indian Abdulla Aboobacker won the silver in the same event.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• At CWG 2022, India won 61 medals (22 gold, 16 silver, 23 bronze).

• The triple jump (hop, step and jump) is a track-and-field jumping event.

NOTE

• The Commonwealth Games are held every four years among nations of the Commonwealth (former British Empire). The 2022 edition was hosted by Birmingham, England.

question: The Swaraj party was formed within __________ with the thought of contesting elections to enter the legislative councils with a view to obstructing the governance of the colonial government.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Indian National Congress.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Swaraj Party was formed in 1923 within the Indian National Congress by Motilal Nehru and C. R. Das (Chittaranjan Das), after the withdrawal of the Non-Cooperation Movement. Its aim was to enter the legislative councils and obstruct the colonial government from within. (स्वराज पार्टी — कांग्रेस के भीतर)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The leaders who wanted to contest council elections were called "Pro-changers" (Swarajists), while those who opposed it (like Rajendra Prasad, Sardar Patel) were "No-changers".

• C. R. Das became the party's President and Motilal Nehru its Secretary.

NOTE

• The Swaraj Party performed well in the 1923 Central Legislative Assembly elections and used council entry to expose the flaws of British rule.

question: How does salt contribute to the preservation of food?
option_2: By inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis.
option_3: By reducing the pH of the food.
solution_text:
The correct answer is By inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Salt preserves food by inhibiting the growth of microorganisms through osmosis. A high salt concentration draws water out of microbial cells (and out of the food), creating a hypertonic, dry environment in which bacteria, moulds and fungi cannot survive or multiply. (परिरक्षण — परासरण द्वारा)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• This is why salting/curing is used to preserve items like fish, meat and pickles.

• Sugar preserves food (jams/jellies) by the same osmotic principle.

NOTE

• Other food preservation methods: refrigeration, freezing, canning, dehydration (drying), pasteurisation, adding preservatives (e.g., sodium benzoate) and vacuum packing.

question: The 'Mahawat' term is associated with which season in North-West India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Winter rainfall.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Mahawat" (or Mahawat/Mahawut) refers to the light winter rainfall received in North-West India (Punjab, Haryana, western UP) during the winter season. (महावट — शीतकालीन वर्षा)

• This rain is caused by the Western Disturbances — temperate cyclones originating over the Mediterranean Sea.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The Mahawat rain is very beneficial for the Rabi crops, especially wheat, as it provides moisture during the growing season.

• Western Disturbances also bring snowfall to the Himalayas in winter.

NOTE

• Rabi crops (wheat, barley, gram, mustard) are sown in winter (Oct–Dec) and harvested in spring (Mar–Apr). Kharif crops (rice, maize, cotton) depend on the southwest monsoon.

question: In his autobiography, Babur described his interest in planning and laying out formal gardens, placed within rectangular walled enclosures and divided into four quarters by artificial channels. These gardens are known as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chahar Bagh.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The formal Mughal gardens, laid out within rectangular walled enclosures and divided into four quarters by artificial water channels/walkways, are known as "Chahar Bagh" (literally "four gardens"). Babur, who loved gardens, described these in his memoirs, the Baburnama (Tuzuk-i-Baburi). (चारबाग शैली)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Chahar" is Persian for "four" and "bagh" means garden.

• Famous examples of Chahar Bagh style: the gardens of the Taj Mahal, Humayun's Tomb and the Nishat/Shalimar Bagh in Kashmir.

NOTE

• Babur (1483–1530) founded the Mughal Empire after the First Battle of Panipat (1526), defeating Ibrahim Lodi. His memoir is written in Chagatai Turkish.

question: Which of the following Census decades in India recorded the highest crude death rate?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1911-1921.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The census decade 1911–1921 recorded the highest crude death rate in India and is called the "Great Divide / Year of the Great Divide" in demographic history, because it was the only decade in which India's population actually declined. (1911-1921 — जनसांख्यिकीय महाविभाजक)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• The high mortality was due to the influenza (Spanish Flu) epidemic of 1918, along with famines, plague and poor health conditions.

• After 1921, India's population grew steadily; 1921 is called the "demographic divide" as growth became continuous thereafter.

NOTE

• The crude death rate is the number of deaths per 1,000 population per year. India's mortality has fallen sharply due to better health care, nutrition and disease control.

question: Which of the following Articles is automatically suspended when an emergency is declared on the grounds of external aggression?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 19.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 358, when a National Emergency is declared on the grounds of war or external aggression, the six freedoms guaranteed by Article 19 are automatically suspended. (अनुच्छेद 19 — बाह्य आपातकाल में स्वतः निलंबित)

• Article 19 is not automatically suspended during an emergency declared on the ground of "armed rebellion" (internal emergency).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Article 19 guarantees six freedoms: speech and expression, assembly, association, movement, residence, and profession/trade.

• Under Article 359, the President may suspend the right to move courts for the enforcement of other Fundamental Rights during an emergency (except Articles 20 and 21, which can never be suspended, as per the 44th Amendment).

NOTE

• Types of Emergency: National (Article 352), State/President's Rule (Article 356) and Financial (Article 360).

question: Rita Mustaphi who is honoured with Mcknight Fellowship of 2023 for her excellent innovation in which of the following Indian Dance Forms?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kathak.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Rita Mustaphi, a distinguished dancer and choreographer, was honoured with the McKnight Fellowship of 2023 for her innovation in the Kathak classical dance form. (कथक — रीता मुस्तफी)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Kathak is one of the eight Indian classical dances, associated mainly with North India, known for rhythmic footwork (tatkar), pirouettes (chakkars) and storytelling (abhinaya).

• The McKnight Fellowship (USA) supports outstanding mid-career artists.

NOTE

• The eight classical dance forms: Kathak, Bharatanatyam, Kathakali, Kuchipudi, Odissi, Manipuri, Mohiniyattam and Sattriya. (Yakshagana is a folk theatre form of Karnataka, not a classical dance.)

question: Padma Shri Pandit Rajeev Tharanath, the famous __________ player is from the state of Karnataka.
solution_text:
The correct answer is sarod.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Pandit Rajeev Taranath, a Padma Shri awardee from Karnataka, was a renowned sarod player of Hindustani classical music. (सरोद वादक — राजीव तारानाथ)

• He was a disciple of the legendary Ustad Ali Akbar Khan.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The sarod is a fretless, plucked string instrument with a deep, resonant tone, prominent in Hindustani classical music.

• Other famous sarod players: Ustad Amjad Ali Khan and Ustad Ali Akbar Khan.

NOTE

• Instrument–artist pairs for SSC: Sitar (Ravi Shankar), Sarod (Amjad Ali Khan), Flute (Hariprasad Chaurasia), Santoor (Shivkumar Sharma), Shehnai (Bismillah Khan), Tabla (Zakir Hussain).

question: At 1 bar pressure, the volume of a fixed amount of hydrogen gas is 2.27 litre. What will be the volume if the pressure is kept at 0.2 bar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 11350 cm³.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• At constant temperature, this is an application of Boyle's Law (P₁V₁ = P₂V₂), which states that the volume of a fixed mass of gas is inversely proportional to its pressure. (बॉयल का नियम)

• Calculation:

◦ P₁V₁ = P₂V₂ → (1 bar)(2.27 L) = (0.2 bar)(V₂)

◦ V₂ = 2.27 ÷ 0.2 = 11.35 L = 11350 cm³ (since 1 L = 1000 cm³).

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• As the pressure is reduced to one-fifth (1 → 0.2 bar), the volume increases five times (2.27 → 11.35 L), confirming the inverse relationship.

• Charles's Law: V ∝ T at constant pressure; Gay-Lussac's Law: P ∝ T at constant volume.

NOTE

• Unit conversion: 1 litre (L) = 1000 cubic centimetres (cm³) = 1000 millilitres (mL). Boyle's Law holds only at constant temperature.

question: Which of the following is NOT a private sector industry in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited (BHEL).

IMPORTANT POINTS

• BHEL (Bharat Heavy Electricals Limited) is a public sector undertaking — it is owned and controlled by the Government of India, not a private company. (बीएचईएल — सार्वजनिक क्षेत्र)

• It is a Maharatna company and India's largest power-equipment manufacturer.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Dabur, Tata Iron and Steel (TISCO / Tata Steel) and Bajaj Auto are all private sector companies (owned and managed by private individuals/firms).

• In the public sector, ownership lies with the government (e.g., SAIL, ONGC, BHEL, GAIL).

NOTE

• Public Sector Undertakings (PSUs) are graded as Maharatna, Navratna and Miniratna based on their financial performance and autonomy.

question: Select the correct sentence about the water table.
option_1: The lower level of the groundwater layer is called water table.
option_2: Water cannot be found below the water table.
option_3: The water table varies from place to place.
option_4: The water table cannot be changed at a given place.
solution_text:
The correct answer is The water table varies from place to place.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The water table is the upper level of the saturated zone of groundwater — the level below which the soil/rock is fully saturated with water. It varies from place to place (and season to season) depending on rainfall, terrain and water use. (भूजल स्तर — स्थान के अनुसार बदलता है)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Statement A is wrong — the water table is the upper (not lower) level of the saturated zone.

• Statement B is wrong — water (saturated zone) IS found below the water table.

• Statement D is wrong — the water table can change (it falls with over-extraction/drought and rises with recharge/rainfall).

NOTE

• Excessive extraction of groundwater lowers the water table, causing wells to dry up; rainwater harvesting helps recharge groundwater and raise the water table.

question: Brahmo Samaj, the theistic movement within Hinduism, was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in the year __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1828.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Brahmo Samaj was founded by Raja Ram Mohan Roy in 1828 in Calcutta (originally as the Brahmo Sabha). It was a theistic (monotheistic) reform movement that opposed idol worship, casteism and superstitions, and advocated the worship of one formless God. (ब्रह्म समाज — 1828)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Raja Ram Mohan Roy is called the "Father of the Indian Renaissance / Modern India". He played a key role in the abolition of Sati (1829) under Governor-General Lord William Bentinck.

• Later leaders of the Brahmo Samaj: Debendranath Tagore and Keshab Chandra Sen.

NOTE

• Other socio-religious reform movements: Arya Samaj (1875, Dayananda Saraswati), Prarthana Samaj (1867, Atmaram Pandurang), Ramakrishna Mission (1897, Swami Vivekananda).

question: The English novel 'Morning Face' is written by:
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mulk Raj Anand.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The English novel "Morning Face" was written by Mulk Raj Anand, one of the pioneers of Indian English fiction. It is part of his autobiographical series of novels. (मुल्क राज आनंद — 'मॉर्निंग फेस')

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• Other famous works of Mulk Raj Anand: "Untouchable", "Coolie", "Two Leaves and a Bud" and "The Village".

• "Morning Face" won him the Sahitya Akademi Award (1971).

NOTE

• Mulk Raj Anand, R. K. Narayan and Raja Rao are regarded as the trinity of early Indian English novelists. Narayan created the fictional town of Malgudi.

question: If the body of an animal can be divided into two indistinguishable left and right halves through only one plane, then it possesses:
solution_text:
The correct answer is bilateral symmetry.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• "Bilateral symmetry" means the body can be divided into two identical (mirror-image) left and right halves by only ONE plane (the sagittal plane). (द्विपार्श्व सममिति)

◦ Examples: humans, insects, fish, most animals.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• "Radial symmetry" — the body can be divided into similar halves by any plane passing through the centre (e.g., starfish, jellyfish, sea anemone).

• "Asymmetry" — no plane divides the body into equal halves (e.g., sponges (Porifera), Amoeba).

NOTE

• Bilateral symmetry is associated with cephalisation (concentration of sense organs at the head end) and directional movement. Adult echinoderms (starfish) show radial symmetry but their larvae are bilaterally symmetric.

question: Which volume of the 'Akbar-Nama' is known as Ain-i-Akbari and deals with Akbar's administration, household, army and the revenues and geography of his empire?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Third.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The third volume of the "Akbarnama", written by Abul Fazl, is known as the "Ain-i-Akbari". It is an administrative and statistical record that deals with Akbar's administration, household, army, revenues, and the geography of his empire. (आईन-ए-अकबरी — तीसरा खंड)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Akbarnama has three volumes: the first covers Akbar's ancestors and early years, the second narrates the events of his reign, and the third (Ain-i-Akbari) is the administrative gazetteer.

• Abul Fazl was one of the Navaratnas (nine gems) of Akbar's court.

NOTE

• The Akbarnama was written in Persian. It is a key source for the history of the Mughal Empire under Akbar.

question: Kelucharan Mohapatra is associated with which of the following dances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Odissi.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra was a legendary exponent of the Odissi classical dance form of Odisha. He is credited with reviving and popularising Odissi in the modern era. (ओडिसी — केलुचरण महापात्र)

• He was awarded the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• Odissi is known for its graceful tribhanga (three-bend) posture and chowk stance, and themes drawn from the Gita Govinda of Jayadeva.

• "Fugdi" (Goa) and "Bihu" (Assam) and "Dumhal" (Kashmir) are folk dances, not classical.

NOTE

• Famous disciples of Kelucharan Mohapatra include Sanjukta Panigrahi, one of the first women to popularise Odissi on the global stage.

question: Before the introduction of Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), what type of surveys did the National Statistical Office (NSO) conduct for employment and unemployment indicators in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Quinquennial surveys.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Before the Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) was launched in 2017, the National Statistical Office (NSO) (earlier NSSO) conducted quinquennial (once every five years) surveys to measure employment and unemployment indicators. (पंचवर्षीय सर्वेक्षण)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• "Quinquennial" means occurring once every five years.

• The PLFS now provides employment data annually (for rural + urban) and quarterly (for urban areas), giving more frequent and timely data.

• Key labour indicators: Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR).

NOTE

• Time-period terms: biennial (every 2 years), triennial (every 3 years), quinquennial (every 5 years), decennial (every 10 years — like the Census).

question: Under Article 165, the Governor appoints a person who is qualified to be appointed as a Judge of a High Court to be the __________ for the State.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Advocate-General.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Under Article 165, the Governor of a state appoints the Advocate-General — a person qualified to be a Judge of a High Court — as the highest law officer of the State. (महाधिवक्ता — अनुच्छेद 165)

• The Advocate-General advises the State Government on legal matters and performs legal duties assigned by the Governor.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• The Advocate-General holds office during the pleasure of the Governor and has the right to speak in the state legislature (but cannot vote).

• The corresponding office at the Union level is the Attorney-General of India (Article 76), appointed by the President.

NOTE

• Constitutional law officers: Attorney-General (Art. 76) for the Union; Advocate-General (Art. 165) for a State; the CAG (Art. 148) audits government accounts.

question: Who among the following was a contemporary of Buddha, but is not considered the first founder of the religion?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahavira Swami.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Mahavira Swami (Vardhamana Mahavira) was a contemporary of Gautama Buddha, but he was not the founder of Jainism — he was the 24th and last Tirthankara. Jainism's origins are traced to the first Tirthankara, Rishabhanath (Adinath). (महावीर — 24वें तीर्थंकर, संस्थापक नहीं)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Mahavira (599–527 BCE) was born at Kundagrama (near Vaishali); he attained Kaivalya (omniscience) and preached the Five Vows — Ahimsa, Satya, Asteya, Aparigraha and Brahmacharya (the fifth added by Mahavira).

• The 23rd Tirthankara, Parshvanath, is regarded as a historical figure who preceded Mahavira.

NOTE

• Jainism has two main sects: Digambara (sky-clad) and Svetambara (white-clad), a division associated with Bhadrabahu and the famine that led to migration south.

question: The shotgun (in the shooting sport) is a __________ gauge having a calibre of 18.5-millimetres (The gauge is a unit of measurement for firearms).
solution_text:
The correct answer is 12.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• In the shooting sport, the standard shotgun is a 12-gauge firearm, which has a bore (calibre) of about 18.5 millimetres. (12 गेज शॉटगन)

• "Gauge" (or bore) is the unit indicating the internal diameter of a shotgun barrel.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

Additional Information

• Shotgun events in Olympic/ISSF shooting include Trap, Double Trap and Skeet.

• The lower the gauge number, the larger the bore (e.g., a 10-gauge barrel is wider than a 12-gauge).

NOTE

• Shooting is divided into three disciplines: Rifle, Pistol and Shotgun. India's Olympic shooting medallists include Abhinav Bindra (10 m Air Rifle gold, 2008).

question: Who among the following was appointed as the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in May 2023?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Praveen Sood.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• Praveen Sood, a senior IPS officer (Karnataka cadre), was appointed the Director of the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) in May 2023. (सीबीआई निदेशक — प्रवीण सूद)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

Additional Information

• The CBI is India's premier investigating agency, established in 1963 under the Ministry of Personnel (functions under the DSPE Act, 1946).

• The CBI Director is appointed by a three-member committee consisting of the Prime Minister, the Leader of the Opposition and the Chief Justice of India (or a Judge nominated by the CJI), with a fixed two-year tenure (as per the Lokpal Act / Vineet Narain case).

NOTE

• The CBI is often called the "premier investigating police agency in India"; it also serves as the National Central Bureau of India for INTERPOL.

question: Which day is celebrated as International Day of Non-Violence?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2nd October.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The International Day of Non-Violence is observed every year on 2 October, the birth anniversary of Mahatma Gandhi, the apostle of non-violence (Ahimsa). (अंतरराष्ट्रीय अहिंसा दिवस — 2 अक्टूबर)

• It was established by a United Nations General Assembly resolution in 2007.

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• In India, 2 October is celebrated as Gandhi Jayanti, a national holiday.

• Gandhiji's principles of Satyagraha (truth-force) and Ahimsa (non-violence) inspired civil rights movements worldwide (e.g., Martin Luther King Jr., Nelson Mandela).

NOTE

• Other important days: 31 October — National Unity Day (Sardar Patel's birthday) / also Indira Gandhi's death anniversary; 30 January — Martyrs' Day (Gandhi's death anniversary).

question: The Anusandhan National Research Foundation Bill, 2023 was introduced in Lok Sabha on 4 August 2023, which repeals the __________.
option_1: Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2007
option_2: Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008
option_3: Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2009
option_4: Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2006
solution_text:
The correct answer is Science and Engineering Research Board Act, 2008.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• The Anusandhan National Research Foundation (ANRF) Bill, 2023, introduced in the Lok Sabha on 4 August 2023, repeals the Science and Engineering Research Board (SERB) Act, 2008. The ANRF subsumes the SERB. (अनुसंधान राष्ट्रीय अनुसंधान फाउंडेशन — SERB अधिनियम 2008 का निरसन)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

Additional Information

• The ANRF aims to promote research and development (R&D) and foster a culture of research across universities, colleges and research institutions in India.

• It is based on the vision of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020; the Prime Minister is the ex-officio President of its Governing Board.

NOTE

• The ANRF seeks to bridge the gap between research and its practical application, drawing on both government and private funding.

question: Which of the following is the main objective of the DWCRA model of SHGs?
option_1: To provide education opportunities for rural children
option_2: To provide housing support for rural families
option_3: To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women
option_4: To provide healthcare services to rural women
solution_text:
The correct answer is To provide self-employment opportunities for rural women.

IMPORTANT POINTS

• DWCRA (Development of Women and Children in Rural Areas) was a programme whose main objective was to provide self-employment opportunities and income-generating activities for poor rural women, mainly through Self Help Groups (SHGs). (ग्रामीण महिलाओं हेतु स्वरोजगार — DWCRA)

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

Additional Information

• DWCRA was launched in 1982–83 as a sub-scheme of the IRDP (Integrated Rural Development Programme).

• It aimed to improve the socio-economic status of poor women by organising them into groups for credit and skill development.

NOTE

• DWCRA and similar schemes were later merged into the SGSY (Swarnajayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana) and subsequently into the DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana – National Rural Livelihoods Mission).
